frames.title: One whole ribbon
frames.caption: This ribbon is one whole, from start to finish.
frames.alt: One uncut ribbon. Its left end is zero and its right end is one.

frames.title: Make equal parts
frames.caption: Make 5 equal parts. Colour 3 parts from the start.
frames.alt: The same ribbon is divided into 5 equal parts. The first 3 are teal.

frames.title: Meet the fraction
frames.caption: 3/5 is 3 equal steps from zero.
frames.alt: A ribbon with 3 of 5 equal parts coloured aligns with a number line. Point P is 3/5 of the distance from zero to one.

try_it.prompt: How many equal parts make one whole?
try_it.feedback_en: Yes. All 5 equal parts make one whole.
try_it.explain_en: Count every space, including the white spaces. There are 5 equal parts in the whole.
try_it.alt: A ribbon with 3 of 5 equal parts coloured aligns with a number line. Point P is 3/5 of the distance from zero to one.

frames.title: Same-sized wholes
frames.caption: Start with two ribbons of the same length.
frames.alt: Ribbons A and B have exactly the same length and width. Neither is cut.

frames.title: Compare equal parts
frames.caption: Each ribbon has 8 equal parts. Compare the coloured parts.
frames.alt: Both ribbons have 8 equal parts. Ribbon A has 3 teal parts; ribbon B has 5 yellow parts.

frames.title: Write the comparison
frames.caption: 5/8 covers more ribbon than 3/8.
frames.alt: The same equal-sized ribbons show 3/8 and 5/8. The relationship below is 3/8 < 5/8.

try_it.prompt: Which ribbon has more coloured ribbon?
try_it.feedback_en: Ribbon A has more coloured parts of the same size.
try_it.explain_en: Both wholes match. Compare coloured parts, not the colours.
try_it.alt: Two equal-sized ribbons each have four equal parts. Ribbon A has three coloured parts. Ribbon B has two coloured parts.

frames.title: One whole strip
frames.caption: This paper strip is one whole.
frames.alt: One uncut white paper strip. A bracket spans the entire strip.

frames.title: Join equal parts
frames.caption: Colour 2 parts, then 3 more. Each part is still one eighth.
frames.alt: The same strip has 8 equal parts. 2 are teal, the next 3 yellow, and 3 white. Every part is labelled 1/8.

frames.title: Count the eighths
frames.caption: 2 eighths and 3 more eighths make 5 eighths.
frames.alt: The unchanged 8-part strip has 2 teal parts and 3 yellow parts. Below: 2/8 plus 3/8 equals 5/8.

try_it.prompt: We colour more parts. Does each part change size?
try_it.feedback_en: Each part stays the same size.
try_it.explain_en: Colouring more parts changes how many we use. It does not cut the parts.
try_it.alt: The unchanged 8-part strip has 2 teal parts and 3 yellow parts. Below: 2/8 plus 3/8 equals 5/8.

frames.title: Keep the whole
frames.caption: This full paper strip is our original whole.
frames.alt: One uncut white paper strip. A bracket spans the full original length.

frames.title: Take some parts away
frames.caption: Start with 7 shaded parts. Cross out 3. Keep all 10 spaces.
frames.alt: The original strip has 10 equal spaces. 7 are teal. Red crosses mark the last 3 teal spaces. The other 3 spaces stay white.

frames.title: Count the tenths left
frames.caption: 4 tenths remain. The original whole still has 10 equal parts.
frames.alt: All 10 original spaces remain visible. 4 teal parts are uncrossed; 3 teal parts are crossed out. Below: 7/10 minus 3/10 equals 4/10.

try_it.prompt: After taking parts away, what is our whole?
try_it.feedback_en: Keep the original strip as the whole.
try_it.explain_en: Taking parts away does not make a new whole. We still compare with the full strip.
try_it.alt: All 10 original spaces remain visible. 4 teal parts are uncrossed; 3 teal parts are crossed out. Below: 7/10 minus 3/10 equals 4/10.

frames.title: See the whole
frames.caption: All 42 counters make one whole. We want one of six equal groups.
frames.alt: One whole contains exactly 42 counters. The task is to find one sixth of this whole.

frames.title: Make equal groups
frames.caption: Share all 42 equally. Each of the six groups has seven counters.
frames.alt: Six equal groups are arranged in two rows of three. Each group contains seven dots, making 42 counters altogether.

frames.title: Take one and check
frames.caption: Division finds one group. Multiplication checks that six groups rebuild the whole.
frames.alt: One group of seven counters represents one sixth of 42. The equations are 42 divided by 6 equals 7, and 7 times 6 equals 42.

try_it.prompt: For 1/4 of 28 counters, what does the 4 tell us?
try_it.feedback_en: The bottom number tells us how many equal groups make the whole.
try_it.explain_en: Make 4 equal groups. Each has 7 counters; 7 × 4 checks the whole of 28.
try_it.alt: A whole of 28 counters is represented by four equal sections. The size of one section is unknown.

frames.title: Label what is known
frames.caption: Seven centimetres labels one sixth, not the whole ribbon.
frames.alt: A ribbon is divided into six equal parts. Only its first part is labelled 7 cm. A bracket across all six parts asks for the whole.

frames.title: Repeat the same length
frames.caption: Equal parts have equal lengths. Repeat seven centimetres six times.
frames.alt: All six equal sections are now labelled 7. Each section has the same length of 7 cm.

frames.title: Build the whole and check
frames.caption: Multiply to rebuild the whole. Divide the whole to check one part.
frames.alt: Six sections of 7 cm make 42 cm. The calculation is 7 times 6 equals 42. Dividing 42 by 6 gives 7 again.

try_it.prompt: 1/5 of a ribbon is 9 cm. Which calculation rebuilds the whole?
try_it.feedback_en: The 9 cm is one equal part. The whole needs five copies of that length.
try_it.explain_en: Five parts of 9 cm make 45 cm. Check: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 cm.
try_it.alt: A ribbon has five equal parts. One part is labelled 9 cm. The whole length is unknown.

frames.title: Choose the parts
frames.caption: Thirty marbles make the whole. Three fifths means three of five equal parts.
frames.alt: The whole has 30 marbles. A bar is split into five equal parts, and the first three are highlighted as the parts wanted.

frames.title: Find one part first
frames.caption: Divide the whole by five. Every equal part has six marbles.
frames.alt: Thirty marbles are divided into five equal parts. Each of the five sections is labelled 6. Thirty divided by five is six.

frames.title: Combine and check
frames.caption: Three equal parts give eighteen. Rebuild the whole to check the result.
frames.alt: Three of five sections, each worth 6, are highlighted. Their total is 18 marbles. Checking 18 divided by 3, then multiplied by 5, returns 30.

try_it.prompt: To find 3/8 of 40 counters, what should we find first?
try_it.feedback_en: Eight equal parts make the whole. Find the size of one part before choosing three.
try_it.explain_en: One eighth is 5. Three such parts make 15 counters.
try_it.alt: A whole of 40 counters has eight equal sections. The first three sections are selected.

frames.title: Label the known parts
frames.caption: Eighteen centimetres covers three equal parts together. The whole has five parts.
frames.alt: A bar has five equal sections. A bracket labelled 18 cm covers exactly the first three sections. The whole length is unknown.

frames.title: Split the known amount
frames.caption: Share eighteen centimetres across the three known parts. One part is six centimetres.
frames.alt: The same 18 cm bracket covers three equal parts, now each labelled 6. Dividing 18 by 3 finds one part of 6 cm.

frames.title: Rebuild and check
frames.caption: Five parts rebuild the whole. Finding three fifths again checks the known eighteen centimetres.
frames.alt: All five equal sections are labelled 6. They make 30 cm. The check divides 30 by 5, then multiplies by 3, giving the original 18 cm.

try_it.prompt: 2/7 of a ribbon is 16 cm. Which calculation finds one part?
try_it.feedback_en: The 16 cm covers two parts together. Split that known amount into two equal lengths.
try_it.explain_en: One part is 8 cm. All seven parts make 56 cm; that rebuilds the whole.
try_it.alt: A ribbon has seven equal parts. A bracket over two parts is labelled 16 cm. One part is unknown.
